newsitem.title: USA: US soybean, corn harvest behind average pace-USDA.
newsitem.headline: US soybean, corn harvest behind average pace-USDA.

text.p: The U.S. Department of Agriculture on Monday said two percent of the U.S. soybean crop had been harvested as of September 22, behind the average pace of six percent.
USDA also estimated that seven percent of the U.S. corn crop had been harvested, compared to last week's four percent pace and behind last year's 11 percent.
The Agriculture Department said that three percent of soybeans were in very poor condition, 10 percent poor, 32 percent fair, 45 percent good and 10 percent excellent.
It said 33 percent of the soybean crop was dropping leaves, behind the 51 percent average.
The department pegged three percent of the corn crop in very poor condition, eight percent poor, 27 percent fair, 47 percent good and 15 percent excellent.
The department said 37 percent of the corn crop was mature, behind the average of 56 percent.
USDA said the cotton harvest was estimated at 12 percent complete, equal to the average pace, but slightly behind last year's 15 percent harvest rate.
USDA pegged three percent of the cotton crop in very poor condition, eight percent poor, 26 percent fair, 47 percent good and 16 percent excellent.
USDA said 96 percent of the spring wheat crop had been harvested, ahead of the average pace of 86 percent.
